title: Longevity Research Has a Bullshit Problem - Nautilus
gist: Demographer Saul Justin Newman argues that investigating the world's oldest people revealed supposedly solid longevity records to be flimsy, built on impossible ages, lost paperwork and invented biographies. The excerpt is only the opening.

insights.claim: Newman argues that widely accepted longevity cases, when debunked, reveal themselves as hollow, like a plywood movie-set saloon, and that this recurs across the field.
insights.speaker: Saul Justin Newman
insights.so_what: Supercentenarian and longevity datasets may be unreliable; discount conclusions built on them.
insights.locator: You have the illusion of solidity

insights.claim: The subtitle claims impossible ages, lost paperwork and invented biographies become accepted scientific fact in longevity research.
insights.speaker: Saul Justin Newman
insights.so_what: Treat longevity-industry claims skeptically when data come from age records.
insights.locator: How impossible ages, lost paperwork, and invented biographies

insights.claim: Newman says he had this debunking experience regularly once he began investigating the world's oldest people.
insights.speaker: Saul Justin Newman
insights.so_what: Signals a pattern rather than an isolated error.
insights.quote: I had this feeling on a regular basis
insights.locator: I had this feeling on a regular basis
